clinician.trajectory_summary: A 50-year-old male with terminal-stage chronic kidney disease on hemodialysis presented with acute abdominal pain of 24 hours duration with rapidly progressive intensity, accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and abdominal distension. Physical examination revealed a distended tympanic abdomen with generalized tenderness and a large irreductible painless right inguinal hernia (which was ruled out as the cause of obstruction). Laboratory studies showed normal WBC but elevated CRP (170 mg/L). Plain abdominal X-ray demonstrated air-fluid levels consistent with bowel obstruction. CT imaging revealed critical anatomical findings: abnormal duodenojejunal flexure positioned to the right of the midline, caecum in midline transverse position in contact with the anterior abdominal wall, significant small bowel distention, and a transitional zone near the deep inguinal ring. These imaging findings were highly suggestive of caecal volvulus with incomplete common mesentery. Surgical exploration confirmed distended small bowel with no restriction at the deep inguinal ring, ruling out hernia-related obstruction. Pathology examination revealed signs of chronic ileocolic ischemia, consistent with the volvulus-induced compromise of blood supply.
